title: Ferromagnetism
description: In iron, the spins of neighbouring atoms line up of their own accord, until heat shakes them apart above a critical temperature. Unlocks the Ferrite Magnet.

puzzle.goal: Above a critical temperature the spins in iron no longer line up by themselves, but an applied field still lines them up a little, more easily the closer the iron is to that temperature. Write the susceptibility χ, with C a constant of the material and T_c the critical temperature.
puzzle.name: Curie-Weiss law
puzzle.ask: Find χ for iron at @{T} K, with C = @{C} K and a critical temperature X of @{X} K.
puzzle.method: Mean-field theory: each spin feels the applied field plus a field proportional to the average magnetisation of its neighbours. Solve for the magnetisation per unit applied field.
